allowed_claims: This repository defines a specification and proof boundary for selected legal-reasoning structures.
The four current slices are closed only within their canonical schema, DDL core, Horn-to-AAF contract, and certificate-checker boundary.
Lean source files are the authority for formal statements; runtime correctness needs separate evidence.
Reports and papers are explanatory artifacts, not proof certificates.
Unknown, skipped, timed-out, or unavailable verification remains fail-closed.
forbidden_claims: Do not claim that the full runtime is formally proved by Lean.
Do not turn an LLM candidate into a verified fact without source-bound verification.
Do not treat Python tests, sampled enumeration, or AI audit text as a Lean proof.
Do not change DecisionStatus, checker acceptance, verified_fact gates, or attack/exception/priority semantics from documentation.
Do not present stale reports as current release evidence.
Do not claim LSC-derived runtime metadata proves source truth, legal truth, runtime soundness, or substantive legal outcomes.
Do not claim fact trust envelopes, downgrade labels, provenance fields, derived taint, renderer firewalls, conflict certificates, or review packets change formal acceptance.
runtime_boundary_notes: The 2026-07-03 juris-calculus absorption of transferable LSC ideas is recorded as a runtime metadata and disclosure-boundary event.

Transferable runtime ideas include fact trust envelopes, USER_ASSUMED/DISPUTED/UNKNOWN downgrade handling, HYPOTHETICAL_RESULT/DEGRADED_TO_AUXILIARY/CONFLICT certificate metadata, used_fact_keys, used_rule_ids, source_snapshot_ids, provenance, derived taint, renderer firewalls, cross-module IO declarations, conflict certificates, review packets, and boundary tests.
These runtime metadata fields are not added to canonical_types, do not extend the public slices, and do not create new theorem declarations.
